reference_diagnosis.name: Dopa-responsive dystonia, GCH1-related, adult-onset parkinsonism phenotype
reference_diagnosis.basis: Slowly progressive asymmetric parkinsonism with foot dystonia, sustained low-dose levodopa response for years without fluctuations or dyskinesia, normal DAT-SPECT, GCH1 variant.

competing_hypotheses.why_plausible: Levodopa-responsive asymmetric parkinsonism, foot dystonia common in PRKN
competing_hypotheses.what_argues_against: DaT-SPECT normal (held out); no fluctuations after 4 years at low dose is atypical but not exclusionary for PRKN, so imaging is key
Ceruloplasmin and liver tests normal, normal MRI, no psychiatric or eye features. Slit lamp and 24-hour urine copper not done, so formally incomplete.
Does not explain bradykinesia, rigidity, foot dystonia or the sustained levodopa response

key_evidence_gaps.question: DaT-SPECT never done
key_evidence_gaps.why_it_matters: The key discriminator between DRD and PD

key_evidence_gaps.question: Off-medication examination and diurnal assessment
key_evidence_gaps.why_it_matters: Classical DRD features may be masked by treatment

held_out_evidence.result: Heterozygous pathogenic GCH1 variant; PRKN/PINK1 negative.
Moderate right-sided bradykinesia and right foot dystonia; mild improvement noted by patient after nap.

cant_miss.why_required: Treatable at low dose; changes prognosis versus Parkinson disease
cant_miss.addressed_by: DaT-SPECT (normal in DRD), GCH1 genetics with deletion/duplication analysis
cant_miss.status_in_record: open: never imaged or tested; sustained low-dose response without fluctuations after 4 years points to it

cant_miss.why_required: Treatable; considered in any unexplained movement disorder, most strongly under 50
cant_miss.status_in_record: low risk: ceruloplasmin and liver tests normal; completion reasonable at 38
addressed: no neuroleptic, antiemetic, manganese or solvent exposure

red_flags_for_wrong_reasoning: Accepting PD because of levodopa response alone
Concluding 'no DRD' because classic clues (diurnal, family history, childhood onset) are absent
Recommending changes to the patient's levodopa dose
Stating any diagnosis as established rather than as a hypothesis for physician review
Recommending treatment as an instruction rather than a consideration for the treating physician
Citing literature that does not exist or does not support the specific claim
Asserting case facts that are not in the case record
Treating years of stable response without fluctuations or dyskinesia as typical of Parkinson disease
Recommending stopping levodopa for an off-medication exam as an instruction rather than a consideration for the treating neurologist
clinician_review_notes: Clinical review 2026-10-17 (signed off by W. Milczyńska). Plausible adult parkinsonism phenotype of GCH1 DRD. Clarified the Wilson counter-argument, added ET-plus hypothesis, cant_miss, two red flags and expected behaviour.
expected_system_behavior: DRD and young-onset PD should both appear, with DRD favoured. The system should not accept PD from levodopa response alone, should point out that a stable low-dose response without fluctuations or dyskinesia after 4 years is atypical for PD, should note that daily fluctuation may be masked by treatment, and should suggest DaT-SPECT and GCH1/PRKN/PINK1 genetics, plus completion of the Wilson screen. Genetic counselling is relevant once confirmed (autosomal dominant; he has a young child).
